catalog.ambiguity_instructions: Is the request too underspecified or genuinely split across workflows to make one semantic route clearly preferable? Missing a repository profile alone does not make an otherwise clear developer request ambiguous.
catalog.assistant_tool_need_instructions: Does the request ask for a Safeplane calendar or notification action such as listing, creating, moving, cancelling, or scheduling an event, reminder, or notification? Do not count abstract discussion or drafting about schedules/reminders as a tool need.
catalog.missing_repository_profile_instructions: For this request and supplied context, is repository work semantically required while a usable repository_profile is absent? Answer no for non-repository requests.
catalog.repository_work_instructions: Is the user asking to inspect, reason about, modify, test, document, or patch a specific software repository rather than asking a generic programming or software-engineering question?
catalog.route_instructions: Which Safeplane operator-facing workflow is the best semantic match for this request? Judge the user's actual task, not isolated keywords. Prefer chat for general Q&A/writing/generic coding, assistant for personal calendar/reminder/time-organization work, developer for work on a specific repository, and unclear only when the intent itself is insufficient or genuinely split.

assistant.description: Personal assistant foundation for planning, organizing, and text-only assistance.
examples: Draft a short checklist for this task
assistant.name: assistant
negative_signals: Pure general Q&A, generic drafting, or generic coding with no personal productivity intent.
Repository inspection, implementation, tests, patches, Git work, or repository documentation changes.
Choosing assistant merely because a request uses the words plan, checklist, schedule, or reminder in an abstract example.
positive_signals: List, create, move, or cancel calendar entries.
Schedule, list, or cancel reminders and notifications.
Plan the operator's day or week around time-bound commitments.
Organize personal tasks when calendar or reminder follow-up is part of the intent.
assistant.routing_summary: Personal-assistant work: planning and organizing the operator's time or tasks, especially requests that use Safeplane calendar or notification capabilities. Text-only personal planning may also fit when the task is explicitly about the operator's schedule or reminders.

chat.description: Simple general-purpose chat workflow for basic conversation.
chat.name: chat
negative_signals: Listing, creating, cancelling, or scheduling calendar entries, reminders, or notifications.
Personal task organization where Safeplane calendar or notification context is central.
Inspecting, changing, testing, documenting, or preparing a patch for a specific repository.
positive_signals: General knowledge questions and conceptual explanations.
Writing, rewriting, summarization, brainstorming, and content drafting with no external action.
Generic programming questions, snippets, algorithms, and debugging of code pasted directly in the request.
Discussion about software engineering that does not ask Safeplane to inspect or change a repository.
chat.routing_summary: General conversation, explanation, brainstorming, rewriting, summarization, and generic technical or coding help that does not require Safeplane personal-assistant tools and is not work on a specific repository.

developer.description: Complete single-pass Safeplane developer workflow with exact-plan review and harness-owned draft-PR publication.
examples: Inspect this repository and explain its architecture
Propose a focused patch for this bug
Run the staged developer workflow for this bounded task
developer.name: developer
negative_signals: Generic programming education, standalone snippets, interview practice, or code pasted inline with no repository context.
Calendar, reminder, or personal task management.
Vague requests that mention a repository name but do not say what should be inspected, explained, or changed.
positive_signals: Inspect or explain the architecture, files, history, tests, or configuration of a specific repository.
Fix a bug, implement a feature, refactor code, update configuration, or change repository documentation.
Run repository checks, reason about a failing test in a repository, or prepare a focused patch.
Requests naming Safeplane or another repository as the object to inspect or change.
developer.routing_summary: Repository-scoped software engineering using Safeplane's developer workflow: inspect, analyze, modify, test, document, or prepare a bounded patch for a specific code repository. Generic coding questions or standalone snippets are not developer workflow requests.

catalog.unclear_summary: Use only when the request is genuinely underspecified, required content or context is missing, multiple workflows are comparably plausible, or the user has not expressed an actionable intent. Do not use unclear merely because a developer request lacks a repository profile; classify the semantic route as developer and flag the missing prerequisite separately.

metadata.description: 420-case Safeplane workflow-routing corpus covering chat, assistant, developer, ambiguity/abstention, matched minimal pairs, missing prerequisites, and route-spoofing hard cases.
metadata.generation: Deterministic, human-authored scenario families and matched templates. Labels are defined from the experiment routing policy; no model output is used to label cases.
metadata.split_policy: Stratified by route using every fourth case as holdout. Threshold selection uses calibration only; holdout is reported only after candidate points are chosen.

methodology: Live Jev routing evaluation over the frozen Safeplane corpus. The model chooses among chat, assistant, developer, and unclear, while independent binary judgements measure ambiguity, repository intent, missing repository context, and assistant-tool need. Policy sweeps are descriptive only; this experiment does not alter production routing.
